text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic visited Salonika port on Saturday and met Greek Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos.

- Yugoslavia to import 3.5 billion cubic meters of gas worth $300 million as planned in 1997 within the scope of the Yugoslav-Russian barter deal, says director of joint venture firm Progres-trading Toplica Nedeljkovic.
- Textile and leather processing industry facing large problems at beginning of year halting tendency for growth shown at end of last year, says official of Serbian Chamber of Economy.
- A shipment of Zastava cars from Kragujevac left for South Korea. Paper unofficially learbs a joint venture is to be formed for production of some 30,000 cars a year.
- Coal deposits in Kosovo province are worth at least $125 billion, say geologists in a study.
- Serbian Justice Minister Arandjel Markicevic accuses Belgrade electoral commission of ignoringt Serbian legal order and usurping authority of Supreme court.
- Police use water cannon to unblock bridge over Sava river where supporters of opposition coalition gathered.
- Police atttack peaceful protesters with water cannon and batons.
- Belgrade Bar Associatioan says lawyers will halt work until their demands for reinstatement of November 17 local election results are met.
- Over 1,000 elementary and secondary schools in Serbia (out of 2,154) are on strike over unpaid wages and low base salary, say teachers' trade unions.
- Yugoslav parliament starts its regular spring session Monday.
- Montenegrin Parliament Speaker Svetozar Marovic to visit Greece from February 3 to 5.
- Taxi services, rent-a-car agencies and driving schools will be able to purchase 6,000 vehicles with lower duties, not exceeding 21 percent, in 1997, says federal trade ministry.
